name: Huperzine A

lead: Huperzine A is an alkaloid from Chinese club moss. In height-maxxing circles it is used for the added-height payoff people want from higher growth hormone, often alongside growth-hormone-boosting routines.

The theory is that blocking acetylcholinesterase lowers somatostatin, the brake on growth hormone, so more is released. Clinical research has studied it for Alzheimer's disease and cognition, not height, and some forum users dispute the somatostatin link.

paras: People take it as an oral supplement, usually as one piece of a wider height or sleep-and-recovery stack, and often alongside growth-hormone-boosting habits. It is also sold as a nootropic. Users who try it for height typically run it over weeks to months and judge results by how they feel and by growth-plate status rather than any measured outcome.

Reported side effects include mild nausea, dizziness and insomnia. It can interact with other cholinesterase inhibitors and anticholinergic drugs. It is a prescription drug for Alzheimer's in China and sold as a supplement in the US. Growth plates close after puberty, so height gains are not expected in adults.

angle.text: Huperzine A is a club-moss extract that height-maxxers take hoping to lower somatostatin, raise growth hormone and gain height. It is approved for Alzheimer's in China and sold as a nootropic; its research is in cognition, and forum users disagree about the height theory.

lead: Huperzine A is a plant alkaloid isolated from the Chinese club moss Huperzia serrata and a potent, reversible inhibitor of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase, which breaks down acetylcholine [1][2]. Grokipedia states that it has been approved as a prescription drug for Alzheimer's disease in China since 1996 and is sold elsewhere as a dietary supplement [1].

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed mainly in height-maxxing, where some guides pair it with growth-hormone secretagogues on the theory that it lowers somatostatin and so raises growth hormone [3][4]. Other forum users dispute this theory, saying they found no study linking huperzine A to somatostatin inhibition or height [4].
No published human trial has tested huperzine A for height or any other appearance outcome. Clinical research has concentrated on Alzheimer's disease and cognition [5][6][7].
infobox: Oral (supplement); injection formulations in clinical research [11]
Approved in China for Alzheimer's disease, per Grokipedia [1]

paras: Huperzine A belongs to the Lycopodium alkaloids, a group of more than 200 alkaloids from club mosses, several of which inhibit acetylcholinesterase [8]. Grokipedia describes the traditional use of Huperzia serrata in Chinese medicine for bruises, swelling and rheumatism, and notes that the plant is slow-growing and wild harvesting raises sustainability concerns [1].

A 2006 review described huperzine A as a highly specific, reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor with better blood-brain barrier penetration, higher oral bioavailability and longer action than tacrine, donepezil and rivastigmine, and with protective effects on cells in animal models [2]. The crystal structure of acetylcholinesterase bound to huperzine A was published in 1997 [9]. A 2017 review discusses it among traditional Chinese medicine ingredients studied for anti-ageing effects [10].

Registered trials have tested huperzine A in Alzheimer's disease, including a US phase 2 trial of 150 participants and a Chinese phase 2/3 trial of sustained-release tablets with 390 participants [5][6]. Other registered studies cover schizophrenia with cognitive impairment, traumatic brain injury, cocaine dependence, cognition during exercise, presbycusis and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers [7][11][12][13][14][15]. Grokipedia summarises meta-analyses as reporting improvements in cognition and daily living in Alzheimer's disease, with mild side effects such as nausea and dizziness [1]. No studies were found testing huperzine A for height, growth hormone or appearance.

A looksmax.org thread documented a teenager's planned multi-month height-maxxing regimen combining a growth-hormone secretagogue with huperzine A; another user answered that such threads rarely deliver the promised updates [3]. A second thread argued that the somatostatin-inhibition claim had been attributed to huperzine A in a popular height guide in error, confusing it with pyridostigmine, and said the author could find no study linking the two [4]. One reply proposed a chain through acetylcholine and somatostatin as a possible but uncertain mechanism [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org huperzine A is discussed in height-maxxing threads as a growth-hormone aid [3][4].

claims.claim: Huperzine A is a somatostatin inhibitor that raises growth hormone and could add height.
The somatostatin claim is a mix-up with pyridostigmine, so huperzine A does nothing for height.
Raising acetylcholine indirectly lowers somatostatin and so could raise growth hormone.
